transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess they brought me in because... well, at the warehouse. I move freight there. Which is funny because when I was taking classes at the college, I swore I wouldn't do heavy lifting. My dorm room was on the fourth floor and there was no elevator. Carrying a mini-fridge up all those stairs... man, that was a mistake. 

But yeah, at work, they got mad because I keep doing things. Like, I'll just freeze with my arms up right by the forklift. And I copy the beeping sounds it makes, and the hand signals the drivers do. I have to move the boxes in these strange little patterns, too, even when everyone is yelling for me to stop. They yell so loud. My boss has this vein in his neck that pops out when he yells. It looks like a little blue worm. I used to dig for worms in the mud after it rained when I was little... but anyway, they told me I had to come here.
Have you had these kinds of behaviors—freezing in positions, copying sounds and movements—since you were a young child, or is this something new that started more recently?

No, not since I was a kid. The strange behavior at the warehouse, and the confusing talking... that's been happening for about six months now. Yeah, about six months. 

That was right around when they finally fixed the vending machine in the break room. It used to just eat your dollar bills. Just swallow them and give you absolutely nothing. You'd watch George Washington's face just disappear into the little slot. I wonder who draws the faces on the money. It must be a really specific job, you know? Sitting in a government room somewhere just drawing tiny little lines on presidents all day. Do they have to use a magnifying glass for that? My grandfather had a big magnifying glass with a wooden handle that he used to read the newspaper. He always read the Sunday comics first. Garfield was his favorite, even though he hated actual cats. Cats make my eyes itch... but yeah, six months.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, head injuries, seizures, or been using any drugs or alcohol around the time these behaviors started six months ago?

No, no sickness or head injuries or seizures or anything like that. I've never hit my head. They make us wear these yellow hard hats at the warehouse anyway, just in case something falls. They're exactly the color of a school bus. I used to hate riding the bus because the seats were made of that weird sticky green vinyl... if you wore shorts in the summer, your legs would peel off them making this loud ripping sound, like duct tape. Duct tape fixes everything, they say. My dad tried to fix the muffler on his truck with duct tape once and it just melted and smelled like burning plastic for a month. 

But no, I don't drink alcohol or do drugs either. Alcohol smells too much like hand sanitizer. They put those giant pump bottles of sanitizer in the break room, and it dries out your knuckles so bad they crack. My mom used to put this thick white lotion on my hands when they cracked, and it smelled exactly like oatmeal. Oatmeal is only good if you put brown sugar in it, but if you put too much, it gets all crunchy. I really don't like crunchy things in the morning... so yeah, no drugs or being sick.
Have you been hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or believing things that others tell you aren't true?

No, I don't... I don't hear anything like that, or see anything that isn't there. People don't tell me I'm believing weird things, either. They just yell about the boxes. They yell so loud it hurts my ears sometimes. My ears used to ring when I went to concerts in high school. We went to this one show in a basement and the speakers were taller than I was. The guy playing bass had this huge beard, like a lumberjack. Lumberjacks wear those red flannel shirts, right? I bought a red flannel shirt once from a thrift store, but it smelled like mothballs and I could never wash the smell out. Mothballs are so weird... they just evaporate into nothing. Where does the ball go? It just turns into bad-smelling air. Air is invisible, which is crazy when you think about it, because we're just walking around in it all the time... but no, no voices or seeing things.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like unexplained weight loss or gain, tremors, muscle stiffness, or being told you have a thyroid or other medical condition?

No, I haven't noticed any weight changes or stiffness or... what was the other thing? Thyroid? No, nobody's told me I have anything like that. I haven't been to a regular doctor in a long time, actually. The last time I went was for a physical for college, back when I was still going to classes. I had to sit on this paper on the examination table, and every time I shifted my weight, it would crinkle so loud. It sounded exactly like when you crumple up wax paper to put in a baking pan. My grandma used to bake these incredible lemon bars, and she always lined the pan with wax paper. She said it was the secret to getting them out without ruining the crust. The crust was always the best part, all buttery and crumbly. Butter makes everything better, honestly. I tried to make toast in the break room toaster once, but it got stuck and started smoking, so I had to eat it dry. Dry toast is like eating a sponge. Sponges get so gross if you leave them wet in the sink... but yeah, no physical changes or anything.
Over the past six months, have you noticed your mood being unusually elevated, irritable, or 'high' for extended periods of time?

No, I haven't felt high or... unusually elevated. Elevated just makes me think of elevators, or those big orange scissor lifts we have to use at the warehouse to reach the top pallets. I hate going up on those things because the metal grate floor lets you see straight down to the concrete. Concrete is so hard on your knees if you stand on it all day. My uncle used to pour concrete for driveways, and he always said you have to smooth it out before it cures or it's ruined forever. Curing meat takes a long time too, like beef jerky. I tried making beef jerky in the oven once but I left it in too long and it just tasted like salty shoe leather. Have you ever noticed how shoes get that weird wear pattern on the heel? I always wear out the outside edge of my left work boot first, it gets all slanted. Slanted floors make me dizzy... but no, my mood hasn't been high or irritable or anything like that.
Do you ever feel that your boss or coworkers are deliberately trying to harm you, control you, or plot against you in some way?

No, I don't... they aren't plotting anything. My boss just cares about moving the pallets and the schedule. He makes us use this old metal punch clock, and it makes this really heavy, loud *kachunk* sound when you put your timecard in. I lost my timecard once and he gave me a temporary one, but it was printed on this really flimsy paper. Paper cuts are the absolute worst, aren't they? I got one right on the webbing between my fingers when I was breaking down a cardboard box last week. Cardboard is mostly just recycled paper anyway, which makes you wonder how many times the same piece of paper has been used. Like, maybe my box used to be a newspaper from the nineties. My dad used to read the newspaper every single morning at the kitchen table, and his fingers would get covered in that gray ink. Ink is so hard to wash off. I tried using that orange pumice soap once, the kind mechanics use, but it just made my hands feel like sandpaper. Sandpaper comes in all those different grits, and the really fine one almost feels soft if you rub it the wrong way... but no, nobody at the warehouse is trying to control me or hurt me or anything.
Have you noticed that when you're talking, your thoughts tend to jump quickly from one topic to another, and do you find it hard to stay focused on the original question?

Yeah, I guess... I guess that happens sometimes. Like, my supervisor will ask me which pallets are supposed to go on the outgoing truck, and I'll start trying to explain the load sheet to him, but then... I don't know, my words just kind of jump. I'll start talking about the load sheet, and then suddenly I'm talking about my old house, the one with the big porch. We used to go fishing right behind that house. Fishing is mostly just waiting around, honestly. You sit there with the bobber in the water, and the water is so still, just reflecting the clouds. The church ladies used to bring these big cardboard boxes of clothes to the house, too, the same kind of boxes we use at the warehouse. Church boxes always smelled like mothballs and old perfume. Old perfume gets that weird, sharp smell if it sits on a dresser for too long... but yeah, by the time I'm done talking, my supervisor just looks at me and nobody has any idea what I meant or which pallets are supposed to go on the truck.

Aside from freezing with your arms up, have you ever found yourself unable to speak at all for a while, resisting when someone tries to move your body, or holding an unusual position for a long stretch of time even if it's uncomfortable?

I guess they brought me in because I keep doing that at the warehouse... freezing with my arms up by the forklift. Sometimes I just hold them there, like I can't put them down. And I'll copy the beeping sounds the forklift makes when it backs up. *Beep, beep, beep.* And I do the hand signals the drivers use, too. I also started moving the boxes in these strange little patterns, like they have to be stacked just right, even when everyone is yelling for me to stop. Yelling is so loud in that warehouse. The acoustics are terrible because of the high metal ceilings. Metal ceilings always make me think of rain. When it rains on a tin roof, it sounds like a thousand tiny drums playing all at once. I used to have a drum set when I was in middle school, just a cheap snare and a cymbal. Cymbals get dull if you don't polish them, but the polish smells like ammonia. Ammonia is what they use in window cleaner, right? The blue kind. Blue is my favorite color, especially the dark blue of the sky right before it gets completely dark... but yeah, they get really mad when I don't stop moving the boxes like that.
Have people told you that you laugh, smile, or act silly at times that don't seem to fit the situation, or that your facial expressions seem flat or don't match what you're feeling?

I don't... I haven't really noticed anyone saying that to me. I mean, I smile sometimes, I guess. Usually when I'm on my break outside by the loading dock. There's this one stray cat that comes around the dock, a little orange tabby. He's got a torn ear, like he got into a fight with a raccoon or something. Raccoons are actually pretty smart, you know. They have those little hands that look almost human, and they can open latches and jars. My grandma used to keep her flour in these big glass jars with the metal clasp on the side. She made the best biscuits, really flaky, with lots of butter. Butter is so expensive now, though. I saw the price at the grocery store the other day and I couldn't believe it. The grocery store near my apartment always has one cart with a squeaky wheel, no matter which one you grab. It's like, *squeak, squeak, squeak* all down the cereal aisle. Cereal boxes have so much empty space in them, they just fill it with air so it looks bigger... but no, I don't think my face does anything weird or flat. Nobody has mentioned it, anyway.

When your arms are frozen up like that, if someone tries to physically push them back down, do you resist and fight against it, or do they let the other person move them without any effort on your part?

I don't really know, honestly. Nobody really tries to push my arms down when I get like that. They just kind of stare at me or yell. Yelling doesn't really help anything, though. It just makes the air feel thick, you know? Like when it's about to storm in the summer and the humidity is just pressing down on you. Summer storms always roll in so fast in the afternoons. One minute it's sunny, and the next the sky is bruised purple and the wind is whipping the trees around. Trees have such deep roots, it's amazing they don't just pull right out of the ground when the wind hits them like that. Roots go down so far, searching for water. Water pipes in my building are so old, they rattle whenever anyone turns on the shower. It sounds like someone is knocking on the wall from the inside. Knocking on walls is how people in prison communicate, I saw that on a documentary once. Documentaries are way better than regular movies because they're real... but yeah, I don't think anyone has actually tried to move my arms for me. They just leave me there.
Aside from freezing in place, do you ever find yourself actively refusing or resisting when someone asks you to do something or move, even when there's no clear reason to refuse?

No, I don't think I do that. If someone asks me to move, I usually just... well, I don't actively fight them or anything. I mean, the shift supervisor, Dave, he asked me to move a pallet last week, and I did it, eventually. Dave wears these really thick glasses, the kind that make his eyes look huge, like an owl. Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around, which is crazy when you think about the bones in their neck. Bones are mostly calcium, right? That's why they always tell you to drink milk when you're a kid. We used to get milk delivered in actual glass bottles when I was really little, before my parents moved. The milkman would leave them on the porch, and the glass would get all foggy from the cold. I loved drawing little smiley faces in the condensation. Condensation is just water vapor turning back into liquid, it's basic science. I took a science class at the community college before I had to drop out and start at the warehouse. The professor had this weird habit of clicking his pen the whole time he lectured. *Click, click, click.* It drove me insane... but no, I don't really refuse to move or anything like that.

No, I don't... I haven't really experienced anything like that. I don't think so, anyway. I mostly just try to do my job and go home. The forklift I drive at the warehouse has this weird steering wheel that sticks if you turn it too far to the left. Left-handed people are supposed to be more creative, I read that somewhere. My cousin is left-handed and he draws these really detailed pictures of cars. Cars are so complicated now, with all the computer chips in them. You can't even fix them yourself anymore. You used to just be able to open the hood and see the engine and know what was wrong, but now it's all covered in plastic. Plastic is ruining the ocean, there's like a giant garbage patch floating out there the size of Texas. Texas is huge, I drove through it once when I was a kid and it took like two whole days just to get across it. The sky out there really does look bigger, like it stretches further down to the ground. But no, nothing like what you're asking about.
Have you or others noticed any changes in your ability to take care of yourself lately—like keeping up with bathing, changing clothes, or grooming?

I haven't really noticed any changes, no. I mean, I still shower and put on my work clothes. The water pressure at my apartment is really terrible, though. It takes forever just to rinse the shampoo out of my hair. Shampoo always smells like fake fruit, like green apples or something. Real apples don't even smell like that. We used to go apple picking when I was a kid, and the orchards just smelled like dirt and wet leaves. Leaves are everywhere right now, clogging up the storm drains on my street. When the drains get clogged, the water pools up and cars drive through it and splash it all over the sidewalk. Sidewalks in my neighborhood are super cracked, too. The roots from the big oak trees just push the concrete right up. Concrete is actually really fascinating, the Romans invented it, and some of their buildings are still standing after thousands of years. The Colosseum is mostly concrete and stone. I wanted to take a history class on ancient Rome at the community college before I had to leave and get the warehouse job, but the tuition was just too much. But yeah, I don't think I've changed how I take care of myself. I'm doing fine with all the showering and stuff.
Have there been times when you simply stop talking altogether for a while, even when people are trying to get you to respond?

No, I don't think I've ever just stopped talking. I mean, if someone asks me something, I answer them. We have to talk a lot at the warehouse, especially when we're unloading the big freight trucks. We use these heavy-duty walkie-talkies, Motorola ones, I think. The battery life on them is terrible, though. You have to swap the battery packs out like twice a shift. Batteries are actually really bad for the environment if you don't recycle them right, they leak battery acid into the soil. There's this bin at the hardware store where you're supposed to drop them off, but I always see people just throwing regular trash in there instead. People just don't pay attention to signs at all. Like stop signs, people roll through them constantly. I almost got hit by a guy running a stop sign on my bike when I was in high school. My bike was this bright green Schwinn, it had these really thick tires for going on dirt trails. I used to ride it down by the river, and the water was always so brown and muddy looking. Mud is just dirt and water, but it smells different, you know? Like earthy and kind of sharp, almost like copper. But yeah, I don't just stop talking or ignore people, I always answer if they want me to respond.
When you're frozen with your arms up, if someone gently repositions your arm to a different spot, does it just stay there in the new position on its own, as if it were made of wax?

I don't think I've ever been frozen with my arms up like that. That sounds weird. I mean, I have to use my arms all the time at work, lifting boxes and moving pallets around. We get these wooden pallets that are always splintering, and you have to wear these thick leather gloves so you don't get a piece of wood stuck in your hand. I got a splinter once that got super infected, my whole thumb swelled up and turned purple. Purple is a weird color, it's not really in nature very much except for some flowers and maybe eggplants. I tried to grow eggplants on my balcony once, but the squirrels ate them before they even got big. Squirrels are everywhere around my apartment, they run across the power lines like little acrobats. Power lines always hum if you stand right underneath them and listen really closely. It's this low buzzing sound, kind of like a refrigerator. My fridge is making this awful rattling noise right now, I think the compressor is going bad. But no, my arms don't freeze up or stay in weird positions like wax.

Doctor: Do you sometimes find yourself just staring blankly into space without blinking, almost like you're completely checked out of your surroundings?

Patient: Staring blankly? I don't know, maybe sometimes when I'm tired, but I don't think I just check out like that. Being tired is the worst, though. Sometimes after a long shift at the warehouse, my eyes just feel so heavy, like someone put sand in them. Sand gets everywhere if you go to the beach, it's impossible to clean out of your car. My buddy had this old Honda Civic, and we took it to the coast once, and I swear there was still sand in the floor mats three years later. Floor mats in cars are always so poorly designed, they slide around and bunch up under the pedals. It's actually really dangerous, you could get the gas pedal stuck and just crash right into something. Crashes on the highway are always so bad because everyone is going way too fast. People are always in such a rush to get everywhere, but then they just end up sitting at a red light anyway. Red lights seem to last forever when you're late for something. I was late for my shift last week because the bus just never showed up. Public transit in this city is a joke, they keep cutting the routes. But yeah, I don't think I just stare without blinking or anything like that. I blink normally, I guess.
